ads_analysis.account_level_diagnosis: The account is overwhelmingly rank-constrained in non-brand: the three in-scope non-brand search campaigns are capturing only 5–7% search impression share while losing 93–95% to rank, despite budget not being the limiter (0% lost to budget and only ~56–59% budget utilization). Auction evidence corroborates you’re routinely not in top placements (15.2% top-of-page vs competitors’ 73.2%) and are outranked most of the time (9.1% outranking share). Fixes should prioritize improving eligibility to win auctions (bids + quality/intent alignment), and cutting/isolating low-intent spend that drags efficiency while you try to buy rank.
notable_patterns: Non-brand search campaigns have extremely low reach driven by rank loss, not budget: Auto IS 6% with 94% lost to rank (0% lost to budget); Home IS 5% with 95% lost to rank; Life IS 7% with 93% lost to rank, all with only ~56–59% budget utilization.

Auction positions are consistently weak versus named competitors: avg top-of-page rate is 15.2% for you vs 73.2% for competitors, with only 9.1% outranking share; Nordkreuz Assurance is above you 96.5% of the time while it hits 82.6% top-of-page.

There are “good” keywords that still barely serve, signaling Ad Rank/bid pressure in competitive auctions: e.g., "auto insurance germany" QS 9.0 but only 5.0% impression share (95% lost to rank); "home insurance cost" QS 8.5 with 5.5% IS (94.5% lost to rank).

Meaningful waste/intent mismatch exists inside search: "insurance company phone number" (QS 3.0) spent 2,605.80 with cost/conv 1,371.47; "what is life insurance" (QS 4.5) spent 858.99 with cost/conv 613.56—these soak budget while the core quote/comparison terms can’t win rank.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Reach is severely constrained by rank (6% impression share; 94% lost to rank; 0% lost to budget) while efficiency is poor (ROAS 0.7) and budget isn’t being fully used (57.2% utilization). This points to Ad Rank pressure in auctions plus query mix dragging performance.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Concentrate spend and bidding power on high-intent quote/comparison terms (e.g., "car insurance quote", "auto insurance germany") and aggressively exclude/segment low-intent informational/job/phone-number traffic so you can bid to top-of-page on the terms that can pay back.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: This campaign is almost not participating (5% impression share; 95% lost to rank; 0% lost to budget) and has weak quality foundations (avg QS 4.1) alongside ROAS 0.75. The combination suggests both Ad Rank and relevance/LP alignment problems.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Rebuild around a tight set of commercial-intent ad groups/landing pages (pricing/quote intent) and reduce exposure to process/claims queries (e.g., "home insurance claims process" QS 4.0; cost/conv 244.45) to lift QS and support higher position at sustainable CPCs.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Life is the worst quality baseline (avg QS 2.0) with 7% impression share and 93% lost to rank (0% lost to budget), so it’s structurally unable to win auctions; ROAS is only 0.89. You’re paying for broad education intent (e.g., "what is life insurance") while failing to secure visibility on comparison intent.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Split informational vs quote/comparison intent; pause or heavily downbid educational keywords, and rebuild RSA/LP relevance around comparison/quote themes to lift QS from ~2 toward mid-single digits before attempting to buy more volume.

recommendation_cards.title: Reallocate and bid up on the highest-intent non-brand terms to buy top-of-page share
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Across non-brand search, impression share is only 5–7% while 93–95% is lost to rank (Auto: 6% IS / 94% lost to rank; Home: 5% / 95%; Life: 7% / 93%), with 0% lost to budget and only ~56–59% budget utilization. You’re also rarely in premium placements (15.2% top-of-page for you vs competitors’ 73.2%), indicating you’re not bidding/winning high enough in auctions even when demand exists.
recommended_steps: Create a dedicated high-intent segment (quote/comparison/pricing) using the proven strong terms (e.g., "car insurance quote", "auto insurance germany", "home insurance cost", "life insurance comparison") and apply a more aggressive bid/targeting posture there.
Move budget out of low-intent ad groups/keywords (see waste list below) into the high-intent segment so you can sustain higher first-page/top-of-page eligibility.
Monitor position vs the four named competitors and iterate bids until top-of-page rate meaningfully improves (don’t increase spend uniformly; concentrate it where intent is commercial).
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Top-of-page rate rising from 15.2% toward 25–30%+ while rank-lost impression share in non-brand falls from ~93–95% toward <80%.

recommendation_cards.title: Stop paying for low-intent queries that are crushing efficiency while you’re rank-limited
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Several low-quality/low-intent keywords are consuming meaningful spend at extreme cost/conv: "insurance company phone number" (QS 3.0) spent 2,605.80 with cost/conv 1,371.47; "home insurance claims process" (QS 4.0) spent 2,248.95 with cost/conv 244.45; "what is life insurance" (QS 4.5) spent 858.99 with cost/conv 613.56. Meanwhile, core commercial terms with high QS still can’t serve due to rank loss (e.g., "auto insurance germany" QS 9.0 but only 5% IS; 95% lost to rank).
recommended_steps: Add/expand intent negatives for support/servicing and research intent (e.g., phone number, claims process, what is, definition, wiki) in non-brand campaigns, or isolate these into a separate low-bid educational campaign if they’re strategically required.
Pause or sharply reduce bids on the named high-cost/low-conversion keywords until they meet a defined CPA ceiling.
Use the freed spend to support bids/coverage on quote/comparison terms where you actually want to win auctions.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Cost/conv on non-brand moving down materially from the worst outliers (e.g., eliminate 1,371.47 cost/conv traffic) while conversions hold or improve as spend shifts to quote/comparison intent.

recommendation_cards.title: Fix Life/Home relevance to lift Quality Score from structurally low levels
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Average quality score is particularly weak in Life (avg QS 2.0) and Home (avg QS 4.1), and both are almost entirely blocked by rank (Life 93% lost to rank; Home 95%). Even with decent ad strength coverage (80% of ads rated Good/Excellent), these QS levels will keep Ad Rank uncompetitive versus rivals that appear top-of-page ~73% of the time.
recommended_steps: Rebuild ad groups tightly by product + intent (e.g., “life insurance comparison/quote”, “home insurance cost/quote”) and align landing pages to the same intent terms in the headline and above-the-fold content.
Write new ads specifically for comparison/quote themes (pricing, quote, compare, switch) and avoid mixing informational “what is/claims process” intent in the same ad groups.
After restructuring, re-evaluate QS distribution and only then scale bids; otherwise you’ll pay more CPC for the same low position.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Avg QS in Life moving off ~2.0 toward 4.0+ (and Home from ~4.1 toward 5.0+) alongside a reduction in impression share lost to rank.

recommendation_cards.title: Cut competitor-brand ‘zero-click’ leakage; keep only what proves it can convert
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Competitor-brand queries account for a large share of impressions with no engagement signal: 35,700 competitor-brand zero-click impressions, and 48.3% of search-term impressions are from zero-click competitor terms (e.g., "bluewave insurance", "harborline mutual", "crestfield direct"). Only one competitor term is shown converting ("nordkreuz insurance quote" with 1.0 conversion).
recommended_steps: Add exact/phrase negatives for competitor brands that generate zero-click volume (Bluewave Insurance, Harborline Mutual, Crestfield Direct) to prevent impression wastage.
Keep a tightly controlled competitor segment only for terms that include strong intent modifiers (e.g., 'quote', 'compare'); start with the proven pattern ("nordkreuz insurance quote").
Review the competitor search-term list weekly and negative out any brand-only terms that continue to show zero-click behavior.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Share of impressions from zero-click competitor terms falling from 48.3% to <20% while overall non-brand conversion volume is maintained or improved.

already_working: Budget is not the limiter right now: every campaign shows 0% impression share lost to budget and only ~51–59% budget utilization (e.g., Auto 57.2%, Home 58.5%, Life 56.2%), so increasing budgets alone won’t fix missed impressions.
Brand search is relatively healthy coverage: 85% impression share with only 15% lost to rank and strong ROAS of 4.7; it’s not the primary drag on account efficiency.

Ad creation isn’t the main bottleneck: 80% of ads are rated Good/Excellent (3 Excellent, 1 Good), suggesting bigger gains will come from auction competitiveness and query/intent control rather than purely rewriting all ads.

market_mapping.why_now_summary: This account’s non-brand search is already demand-available but structurally unable to compete on Ad Rank (93–95% lost to rank). That problem becomes more urgent because (1) Germany insurance search is growing quickly right now (both spend and query demand up QoQ), so the opportunity cost of staying under-ranked is increasing, and (2) competitors are allocating meaningful share to search and showing higher overall category ad intensity—meaning auction pressure is unlikely to ease on its own. Acting now to lift rank (bid + quality/intent alignment) and cut low-intent leakage prevents you from falling further behind as the market heats up.

supporting_facts.fact: Insurance in Germany shows "Spend Growth QoQ" of 18.0% and "Query Demand Growth QoQ" of 12.0%, with "Vertical-Avg Impression Share" at 21.0% (table: "Vertical | Highlighted Market | Spend Growth QoQ | Query Demand Growth QoQ | Vertical-Avg Impression Share", page 5).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: With auctions heating up (spend + demand rising QoQ), a rank-constrained account that’s only capturing ~5–7% impression share risks losing even more coverage unless it improves Ad Rank now (bids and relevance/QS). The 21.0% vertical-average IS also highlights how far below typical coverage the account is today.

supporting_facts.fact: Germany (pilot account market) has "Search Spend Growth QoQ" of 18.0% and "Vertical-Avg Impression Share" of 21.0% (table: "Market | Search Spend Growth QoQ | Vertical-Avg Impression Share", page 7).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Rising search investment in Germany implies increasing competition and CPC pressure. Since budget is not the limiter in the account diagnosis, urgency is to reallocate away from low-intent waste and bid/optimize for rank on the highest-intent terms before the market gets more expensive.

supporting_facts.fact: In the category media mix, "Search" accounts for 38% of "Share of Category Spend" (table: "Channel | Share of Category Spend", page 7).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Because search is a large share of category spend, competitors are likely prioritizing and defending search visibility. A rank-constrained non-brand program will continue to be suppressed unless it becomes more competitive in auctions (higher bids where it pays back + improved quality/intent alignment).

supporting_facts.fact: Bluewave Insurance has 24% "Spend Share" and runs across "Search, Social, Display" with 48 "Active Creatives" (table: "Competitor | Spend Share | Active Creatives | Channels", page 6).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: A major competitor with high spend share and heavy creative activity signals sustained competitive pressure. If your account is already losing 93–95% of non-brand impressions to rank, the cost of waiting is continuing to concede top placements to better-funded competitors.

supporting_facts.fact: Crestfield Direct has 15% "Spend Share" with 29 "Active Creatives" and runs "Search, Social" (table: "Competitor | Spend Share | Active Creatives | Channels", page 6).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Multiple competitors (not just one) are materially invested in performance channels including search—supporting the diagnosis that auction competitiveness is the binding constraint, and strengthening the case to urgently concentrate spend/bids on the highest-intent terms to win rank.

supporting_facts.fact: The keyword "home insurance cost" grows from 100 (Q4 2025) to 119 (Q3 2026), "Growth" 19% (table: "Keyword | Q4 2025 | Q2 2026 | Q3 2026 | Growth", page 6).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: This directly maps to the account’s issue: even strong commercial-intent terms (like cost/quote queries) are where you need top-of-page presence. Demand growth on “home insurance cost” increases the opportunity cost of staying rank-limited and supports acting now to rebuild Home around pricing/quote intent and lift QS/Ad Rank.

supporting_facts.fact: The keyword "life insurance comparison" grows from 100 (Q4 2025) to 109 (Q3 2026), "Growth" 9% (table: "Keyword | Q4 2025 | Q2 2026 | Q3 2026 | Growth", page 6).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Comparison intent is exactly where the account should concentrate bidding power, but Life has very weak QS and is heavily rank-limited. Growing demand for “life insurance comparison” reinforces urgency to split informational vs comparison/quote intent and improve relevance so you can actually enter and win these auctions.

supporting_facts.fact: For the Insurance vertical, "Ad Intensity Index" is 112 with "Reach %" 64% and "Avg Frequency" 3.2 (table: "Vertical | Ad Intensity Index | Reach % | Avg Frequency", page 5).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Above-baseline ad intensity (index 112) supports that competitive pressure is elevated, making a rank-constrained non-brand program even less likely to improve passively. This strengthens the need to act now on Ad Rank levers (bids + quality + intent filtering) rather than waiting for auctions to soften.

why_now_bullets: Germany insurance search is heating up (Spend Growth QoQ 18.0%, Query Demand Growth QoQ 12.0%) — staying under-ranked now gets more expensive later.
You’re currently losing 91.0% of impression share to rank, not budget — meaning the fastest wins are Ad Rank levers (intent tightening + bids + relevance), not bigger budgets.
The category norm is higher coverage (Vertical-Avg Impression Share 21.0%) — you’re competing in a market where others are simply showing up more often.
email_copy.impact_line: That EUR 188,014 isn’t coming from “spending more” — it comes from fixing why non-brand is being shut out of auctions (rank) while budget sits unused, then concentrating spend on quote/comparison intent so you can consistently earn top placements where conversion likelihood is highest.
